subsection.text: The amendments made by subsection (a) shall apply with respect to any determination by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs made on or after the date of the enactment of this Act regarding the misuse of benefits by a fiduciary.

section.header: Exemption of certain transfers
section.text: Section 7364(b)(1) of title 38, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new sentence: Any amounts so transferred after September 30, 2016, shall be available without regard to fiscal year limitations, notwithstanding section 1535(d) of title 31..

section.header: Report and planned actions of the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to address certain high-risk areas of the Department of Veterans Affairs

subsection.text: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, in consultation with the Comptroller General of the United States, shall submit to the Committees on Veterans’ Affairs of the Senate and House of Representatives a report outlining the plan the Secretary has developed and the actions the Secretary has taken to address the areas of concern identified by the Comptroller General for the Department of Veterans Affairs in the 2019 High-Risk List of the Government Accountability Office (GAO–19–157SP) regarding—

paragraph.text: acquisition management; and
managing risks and improving health care.

subsection.text: The report under subsection (a) shall include each of the following:

paragraph.text: Root causes of the areas of concern described in paragraphs (1) and (2) of subsection (a).
Corrective actions and specific steps to address each root cause, including—

subparagraph.text: the progress of the Secretary in implementing those actions and steps; and
timelines and milestones the Secretary determines feasible to complete each corrective action.

paragraph.text: Resources the Secretary determines are necessary to implement corrective actions, including—

subparagraph.text: funding;
stakeholders;
technology; and
senior officials responsible for implementing the corrective actions and reporting results.

paragraph.text: Metrics for assessing progress in addressing the areas of concern described in paragraphs (1) and (2) of subsection (a).
Key outcomes that demonstrate progress in addressing the areas of concern described in paragraphs (1) and (2) of subsection (a).
Obstacles to implementation of the plan that the Secretary identifies.
Recommendations of the Secretary regarding legislation or funding the Secretary determines necessary to implement the plan.
Any other information the Secretary determines is relevant to understanding the progress of the Department toward the removal of the areas of concern from the High Risk List.

Not less than once each year during the implementation period under paragraph (2), the Secretary shall submit to Congress an update regarding implementation of each element of the plan under subsection (b).
The implementation period described in this paragraph begins on the date on which the Secretary submits the report required under subsection (a) and ends on the earlier of the following dates:

subparagraph.text: The date on which the Comptroller General removes the last area of concern for the Department from the most recent High-Risk List of the Government Accountability Office.
The date that is 8 years after the date on which the Secretary submits the plan required under subsection (a).

section.header: Annual report by Secretary of Veterans Affairs on implementation of priority recommendations of Comptroller General of the United States pertaining to Department of Veterans Affairs

subsection.text: Not later than 270 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, and not less than once during each of the subsequent 3 years, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall submit to the Committees on Veterans’ Affairs of the Senate and House of Representatives and to the Comptroller General of the United States a report on the implementation of priority recommendations of the Comptroller General that pertain to the Department of Veterans Affairs.
Each report submitted under subsection (a) shall include, for the period covered by the report, the following:

paragraph.text: The progress of the Secretary in implementing all open priority recommendations of the Comptroller General for the Department of Veterans Affairs.
An explanation for each instance where the Secretary has decided not to implement, or has not fully implemented, an open priority recommendation of the Comptroller General for the Department.
A summary of the corrective actions taken and remaining steps the Secretary plans to take to implement open priority recommendations of the Comptroller General.

subsection.header: Supplement not supplant certain required reports or written statements
subsection.text: The report under this section shall not be construed to supplant any report or written statement required under section 720 of title 31, United States Code.

section.header: Clarification of methods used to monitor compliance with certain limitations on subcontracting
section.text: Section 8127(k)(3)(A) of title 38, United States Code, is amended by striking and any other and inserting or any other.

section.header: Department of Veterans Affairs requirement to provide certain notice to persons filing claims for damage, injury, or death on Standard Form 95
section.text: Not later than 90 days after the date on which a person submits to the Secretary of Veterans Affairs a claim for damage, injury, or death on Standard Form 95, or any successor form, the Secretary shall provide to such person notice of each of the following:

paragraph.text: The benefit of obtaining legal advice concerning such claim.
The employment status of any individual listed on the form.

If the claim involves a contractor that entered into an agreement with the Secretary, the importance of obtaining legal advice as to the statute of limitations regarding the claim in the State in which the claim arose.

subtitle.header: Matters relating to the Chief Financial Officer of Department of Veterans Affairs

section.header: Definitions
section.text: In this subtitle:

paragraph.text: The term appropriate congressional committees means the Committees on Veterans’ Affairs of the Senate and the House of Representatives and the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives.
The term subordinate chief financial officer—

subparagraph.text: includes—

clause.text: the chief financial officer of the Veterans Health Administration, the chief financial officer of the Office of Community Care within the Veterans Health Administration, and all chief financial officers of Veterans Integrated Service Networks within the Veterans Health Administration;

the chief financial officer of the Veterans Benefits Administration and all chief financial officers of organizational subdivisions representing business lines within the Veterans Benefits Administration;
the chief financial officer of the National Cemetery Administration; and
the chief financial officer of the Office of Information and Technology; and

subparagraph.text: does not include the Inspector General.

section.header: Plans for addressing material weaknesses and providing sufficient authority to Chief Financial Officer of Department of Veterans Affairs
section.text: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, and annually thereafter for each of the three subsequent years, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, acting through the Chief Financial Officer of the Department of Veterans Affairs, shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees—

paragraph.text: an action plan, including steps, related timelines, costs, progress, status of implementation, and any updates for fully addressing the material weaknesses of the Department discussed in the Management’s Discussion and Analysis section of the financial statements of the Department submitted to Congress under section 3515 of title 31, United States Code for the year preceding the year during which the report is submitted; and

a plan outlining the steps the Secretary plans to take to address the recommendations of auditors related to entity-level internal controls and to provide sufficient authority to the Chief Financial Officer of the Department to carry out the requirements of section 902 of title 31, United States Code.

section.header: Chief Financial Officer attestation
section.text: Concurrent with the submittal to Congress of the President’s budget request under section 1105 of title 31, United States Code, for fiscal year 2022 and each of the next three subsequent fiscal years, the Chief Financial Officer of the Department of Veterans affairs shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees each of the following:

paragraph.text: A certification of the responsibility of the Chief Financial Officer for internal financial controls of the Department.

An attestation that the Chief Financial Officer has collaborated sufficiently with the subordinate chief financial officers of the Department to be confident in the financial projections included the budget request and supporting materials.

section.header: Chief Financial Officer responsibility for subordinate chief financial officers

subsection.text: In accordance with the responsibilities of the Chief Financial Officer of the Department of Veterans Affairs for the recruitment, selection, and training of personnel to carry out agency financial management functions pursuant to section 902(a)(5)(C) of title 31, United States Code, the Chief Financial Officer or the designee of the Chief Financial Officer within the Office of Management of the Department shall—

paragraph.text: participate in the interview and selection panels of all subordinate chief financial officers; and
give input into the performance plans and performance evaluations of all subordinate chief financial officers.

subsection.text: The requirements under subsection (a) shall terminate on the date that is five years after the date of the enactment of this Act.

section.header: Clarification of delivery of notice of termination of leases of premises and motor vehicles for purposes of relief under Servicemembers Civil Relief Act

subsection.text: Section 305(c)(2) of the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act (50 U.S.C. 3955(c)(2)) is amended—

paragraph.text: in subparagraph (B), by striking or at the end;
in subparagraph (C), by striking the period and inserting ; or; and
by adding at the end the following new subparagraph:

subparagraph.text: by electronic means, including—

clause.text: the direct delivery of material to an electronic address designated by the lessor (or the lessor’s grantee) or the lessor’s agent (or the agent’s grantee);

the posting of material to a website or other internet or electronic-based information repository to which access has been granted to the lessee, the lessor (or the lessor’s grantee), or the lessor’s agent (or the agent’s grantee); and
other electronic means reasonably calculated to ensure actual receipt of the material by the lessor (or the lessor’s grantee) or the lessor’s agent (or the agent’s grantee).

subsection.text: The amendments made by subsection (a) shall apply to delivery of notice of lease terminations on or after the date the enactment of this Act.
